title: Nonlinearity
intro: No amplifier is perfectly linear. Weak nonlinearity can be described by a short power series.

items: Second harmonic: HD2 = a2*A / (2*a1). Even-order terms vanish in a fully differential circuit.
Gain compression: the fundamental is a1*A + (3/4)*a3*A^3. With a3 < 0 the gain falls; it falls by 1 dB at A1dB = sqrt(0.145*|a1/a3|).
Intermodulation: two tones at w1, w2 produce 2*w1 - w2 and 2*w2 - w1, which fall in-band. The third-order intercept point (IP3) has amplitude A_IP3 = sqrt(4*|a1/(3*a3)|); A_IP3 is 9.6 dB above A1dB.
Feedback divides distortion by (1 + loop gain).
Source degeneration trades gain for linearity.

blocks.text: a1 = 10, a2 = 1, a3 = -2, and A = 0.1 V. Find HD2 and HD3 in dB.
